title: Parkour
text: Parkour is a way of moving through a city using only your body. You run, jump, climb and roll over walls, stairs and railings. The goal is to go from one point to another in the most efficient way.
Parkour started in France in the 1990s. A group of young people from the suburbs of Paris, including David Belle, trained together every day. They wanted to be fast and free, like animals.
To do parkour, you do not need any special equipment. You only have to wear comfortable clothes and good shoes. But you have to train a lot: your arms and legs need to be very strong.

The first rule of parkour is safety. Beginners have to start with small jumps near the ground. You do not have to jump from roof to roof! Good traceurs, the people who do parkour, know exactly what they can and cannot do.
Today parkour is popular all over the world, and you can see it in many action films and video games. There are also gyms with special walls and boxes where you can practice safely.

grammar.title: Grammar: have to and do not have to
grammar.rule: Use have to for things that are necessary. Use do not have to when something is not necessary. With he, she and it: has to / does not have to.
rows: You do not have to jump from roofs.
He does not have to buy equipment.
must not ≠ do not have to
items: A traceur ___ to be very strong.
You do not have ___ buy special equipment.
Beginners ___ to start with small jumps.
He ___ have to jump from roofs.
